context_length: Effectively unbounded via T5 relative position bias
summary: A T5-3B protein language model from ProtTrans whose 1024-dim encoder embeddings are a long-standing strong baseline for per-residue and per-protein tasks.
architecture: T5 encoder–decoder (T5-3B) with relative position bias; only the encoder is used to produce 1024-dim per-residue embeddings, mean/attention-pooled here.
pretraining_data: Pretrained on BFD (Big Fantastic Database) then fine-tuned on UniRef50 (~45M sequences).
pretraining_objective: Span-corruption / masked span reconstruction (T5-style denoising, adapted for proteins).
key_innovations: Encoder embeddings capture secondary structure, localization and membrane signal without supervision
Established that large PLMs rival evolutionary (MSA) features for many tasks
when_to_use: A dependable, well-studied 1024-dim baseline; frequently competitive on the enzyme regression tasks in this benchmark. Encoder-only inference keeps it practical.
caveats: Large model; the full checkpoint stores decoder weights that are unused for embedding. Single-sequence; older recipe than ESM-2/ESM-C.
